# eslint-plugin-operability

Guide for AI coding assistants using this plugin in a project. To change the plugin's own source, read https://github.com/ofri-peretz/eslint/blob/main/AGENTS.md instead.

> ESLint production readiness rules — bans debug code and console logging in production, verbose error messages, and process.exit calls.

## Enable it

```bash
npm install --save-dev eslint-plugin-operability
```

Requires ESLint ^8.40.0 || ^9.0.0 || ^10.0.0 and Node >=22.13.0.

Flat config files (`eslint.config.*`) are found by ESLint 8.57 and newer; on ESLint 9 and 10 they are the default.

```js
// eslint.config.mjs
import operability from 'eslint-plugin-operability';

export default [operability.configs.recommended];
```

Each preset is one flat config object: put it in the array as an element, do not spread it. Rule ids are prefixed `operability/`. Add it to the config you already have; do not remove other plugins. TypeScript files need a TypeScript parser in the config (`typescript-eslint`).

## Presets

| Preset        | Rules | Errors | Warnings |
| ------------- | ----- | ------ | -------- |
| `recommended` | 3     | 1      | 2        |

### `recommended`

3 rules:

- `no-console-log` (warn): Disallow console.log with configurable remediation strategies.
- `no-debug-code-in-production` (error): Detect debug code in production.
- `no-verbose-error-messages` (warn): Prevent exposing stack traces to users.

### Rules in no preset

Enable these by name (`'operability/<rule>': 'error'`):

- `no-process-exit`: Prevent usage of process.exit() which can terminate the process unexpectedly.
- `require-code-minification`: Require minification configuration.
- `require-data-minimization`: Identify excessive data collection patterns.
